label: English
title: Quantum Shala
footer: Runs on real Qiskit circuits • QFF 2026 Education Track
shots: Numbers change slightly each run because quantum measurement is probabilistic.
guide_done: Well done! Now look at the picture and the bars, then answer the quiz below. You can also try your own gates.
guide_free: Free play: try any gates. Press Clear to start the guided steps again.
viz_undecided: Spinning: not decided yet. Press "Measure once" to make it land.
viz_certain: Not spinning: the result is already certain.
viz_landed: Landed on {k} this time. Press again: it may land differently.
viz_boxes: The brighter the box, the more often it is found. Press "Measure once" to open one box.
qnote: q0 is the first qubit and q1 is the second. In a result such as 01, the left digit is q0 and the right digit is q1.
ins_one: Always {k}: the result is certain, there is no randomness.
ins_pair: Only {a} and {b} appear, and the two digits always match: the qubits are linked (entangled).
ins_random: The results are spread out: the outcome is not decided until you measure, so it is random.

h.desc: H: puts the qubit in superposition, a 50-50 mix of 0 and 1. Pressing it twice undoes it.

x.desc: X: turns 0 into 1 and 1 into 0, like turning a coin over.

z.desc: Z: changes a hidden sign. Alone you see no change; try H, then Z, then H.

cx01.desc: CX (0→1): flips q1 only if q0 is 1. After H on q0 it ties the two qubits together (entanglement).

cx10.desc: CX (1→0): flips q0 only if q1 is 1. The same idea with the roles swapped.

cz01.desc: CZ: marks box 11 by flipping its hidden sign. Grover uses this to mark the prize box.

L.name: 1. Superposition
L.story: Imagine a coin spinning in the air. Until it lands, it is not yet heads or tails. A qubit is like that: until measured it is a mix of both states.
L.task: Press nothing first: result is always 0. Then press H and watch. Then press H again. What happens?
L.q: After one H gate, how often do 0 and 1 appear?
L.hint: Remember the spinning coin: before it lands, it is neither fully heads nor fully tails. Press H once and read the bars.
L.why: H is the spinning coin. When measured it gives a 50-50 chance.

L.name: 2. Entanglement (a pair)
L.story: Two magic gloves: one in Mumbai, one in Pune. If Mumbai's is left, Pune's is automatically right. Two qubits can be tied together like this.
L.task: Apply H on q0, then CX (0→1). Do only 00 and 11 appear? Do 01 or 10 ever appear?
L.q: Which results appear after making the pair?
L.hint: Think of the gloves: the two always match. Build H on q0 then CX (0→1) and look at which bars are not empty.
L.why: Both qubits always match. Measuring one tells you the other.

L.name: 3. Grover search
L.story: A prize is hidden in one of 4 boxes (here box '11'). The usual way opens 2 to 3 boxes on average. Grover finds the right box in 1 round.
L.task: Press 'Run Grover'. Then try adding the gates one by one yourself. Does 11 appear almost 100% of the time?
L.q: At the end of Grover, how often do we get the prize box '11'?
L.hint: Random guessing among 4 boxes gives 25%. Press 'Run Grover' and read the 11 bar.
L.why: For 4 options one round is enough. More options means a bigger advantage.

circuit_how: Each horizontal line is one qubit (q0, q1). Time moves from left to right.
Each box on a line is a gate you pressed, in the same order as the chips above.
M is the measurement: the qubit is read and becomes a plain 0 or 1.
The line c: stores the measured result. The program repeats the whole circuit 1000 times, and that gives the bars.
step_none: No gates yet: the qubit stays 0.
step_measure: Finally: measure (M) and write down 0 or 1. This is repeated 1000 times.
